chunks: And Ali ibn Isma'il al-Mitham narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who marries his slave-girl to a free man, he said: 'It is not for him to take her back.' As for that which indicates that if he sells her, the buyer has the option between confirming her in the marriage or separating her, this is in addition to what we have previously mentioned, from what he narrated:

key_terms.يَنْزِعَهَا: to take her back / remove her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master sells a slave-girl who is already married to a free man?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a female slave (*umm walad* or otherwise) married to a free man, establishing that the master cannot unilaterally revoke the marriage upon sale. It highlights the buyer's option (*khiyar*) to either uphold the existing contract or dissolve it, reflecting the interplay between manumission status and marital stability in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the protection of the slave-wife's rights within the household structure, ensuring her marital bond is not arbitrarily severed by changes in ownership.
